1.explanation: In the Ruby grammar file the only pattern that attempts to recognize the `?X` character-literal forms lives inside the STRING constant’s variants array.  It uses a single regular expression begin:/\B\?(\\\d{1,3}|\\x[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,2}|\\u[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}|\\?\S)\b/ which covers octal, \xHH, \uHHHH and a catch-all \?\S branch, but misses unescaped slash (`?/`), escaped backslash (`?\\`), Unicode curly/braced notation (`?\u{...}`), non-ASCII characters (`?あ`), and control/meta sequences (`?\C-`, `?\M-`).  To fix the bug you must extend or replace that regex (inside STRING) in the exported function so it also handles these missing cases.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show Highlight.js mis-classifying Ruby’s single-character literal notation (the `?x` syntax) in several cases.  For example `?/` is picked up as the start of a regular expression, `?\\` isn’t recognized as a string at all, non-ASCII (`?あ`) and Unicode curly-brace forms (`?\u{41}`) aren’t highlighted, and control/meta sequences like `?\C-a` or `?\M-a` are not matched.  The expected behavior is that all of these “?X” forms should be lexed as single-character string literals, not regexes or errors.

2.explanation: All character literals in the Ruby grammar are handled inside the STRING definition in ruby.js. One of its variants uses a single regex (“\\B\\?(\\\\\\d{1,3}|\\\\x[…]|\\\\u[…]{4}|\\?\\S)\\b”) to match escaped and simple ?-sequences, but omits raw slash ("?/"), escaped backslash ("?\\"), Unicode curly-brace syntax ("?\\u{…}"), non-ASCII characters ("?あ"), and control/meta forms (e.g. "?\C-a"). To support the missing cases, that variant’s regex (or its surrounding variants) must be expanded to recognize these additional literal forms.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting Ruby code with highlight.js, certain character‐literal notations (e.g. ?/, ?\\, ?\u{1AF9}, ?あ, ?\C-a, etc.) aren’t recognized correctly. The existing grammar treats some of these as the start of regexes or other tokens, leading to broken highlighting or SyntaxError misclassification.
